summary.name: CRT / Analog Video Effects
summary.visualIdentity: An analog-display look built from scanlines, mild color offsets, persistence, screen curvature, and noise. Provenance is explicit. Details scale to output resolution, and distortion stays restrained so main information remains legible.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit guidance limits it to a defined analog-display context. Inferred from suggested combinations: retro game trailers, nostalgic tech stories, and in-world broadcasts or terminals. Other uses are unspecified.
summary.limitations: Avoid persistent flashes, exaggerated noise, rolling noise bars, and analog distortion on modern screens unless requested. Do not apply it over blurred art or stack it with Glitch Art as a second corruption layer. Essential text must stay legible.
summary.palette: Reference-dependent example for new presentation elements only: background #171C24, foreground #E9E5D8, accent #6A9DAA, checked with chroma-js. Approved task or brand colors override these, and gradients are disabled. Source assets stay unrecolored. Contrast is 13.57:1 for foreground on background and 5.713:1 for background on accent, based on two-color checks only.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion derives from seekable composition time, using seeded deterministic noise rather than wall clocks or per-frame grain. Deliberate cuts and reading holds stay intact. Optional motion-020 glitch cut fits CRT only for intentionally disrupted transitions, with bounded, reversible distortion. Motion-012 and motion-015 are optional, and no motion reference is required. Interactive HTML may disable the effect under reduced motion.
summary.audio: No fixed audio is required, and the source assigns no genre, tempo, or voice. Options include restrained sound accents, ambience, music, or silence, chosen from topic and audience, with user-supplied audio honored first. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and picture synchronization.
summary.assetRequirements: Requires high-quality source imagery for postprocessing and authorized footage for video-textured screens. Preload media and wait for decoded frames, since VideoTexture alone does not guarantee export synchronization. Load fonts before rendering. Pixel-art hybrids need native-resolution art. Dimensions, duration, and frame rate are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Best used as a finishing pass over clean content. Pixel art (style-057) may supply on-screen content, upscaled by an integer factor. A diegetic monitor housing (style-065) may frame it, with artifacts confined to the screen surface. Never stack two filters on the same content.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default for scene assembly, timing, synchronization, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. WebGL, GLSL, and Three.js render visuals. Deliverables include the video, source, contact sheet, parameters, and render instructions, with missing assets stated.
